\caption{\textbf{Which quality signal predicts counting error, and when.} AUROC for flagging a photo with a count off by more than 5\% (higher = better; 0.5 = chance) and Spearman $\rho$ between quality and the mean absolute \% error (negative = useful), with 95\% CIs from a bootstrap that resamples the 13 fabrics. Columns 1--5: blur, down-sampling, JPEG, glare and corner-error versions of the 13 legacy crops, scored against the 2019 hand counts (125 of 247, 79 of 117 and 42 of 117 failures). ``No method within 5\%'': none of \ours, log-Gabor, the CNN and GPT-6.1-sol P1 has both counts within 5\%. ``Within fabric'': only conditions of the same crop are compared, so a signal cannot score by recognising intrinsically hard fabrics. Column 6: outputs of five generative restorers (Real-ESRGAN, SeedVR2, InvSR, FLUX.2 [klein], Nano Banana Pro) on $\times$4, $\times$8 and $\times$4+JPEG legacy inputs, against the hand counts (77 of 191 failures). Column 7: restorer $\times$ condition cells (of 27, legacy and full-resolution PickGlass inputs) in which the score of the generative outputs is above bicubic's (paired 95\% CI above zero). Generic IQA (pyiqa) sees the counter's working image (at most 1024\,px, never up-sampled; generated outputs: 768\,px viewing copies). $^{\dagger}$Metric pre-specified; the other generic-IQA metrics and the within-fabric and generative columns are exploratory. $^{*}$Paired 95\% CI of the difference to \ours confidence excludes zero.}
